utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, The Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. No preliminaries were announced, which means that we can immediately proceed to the examination of the next witness. And the Defence calls Mr. Mladjenovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Mr. Stojanovic, you asked for 15 additional minutes to the 30 usual minutes. Well, the Chamber does not object to it. At the same time, we're always carefully considering how you use your time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Mladjenovic, I take it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you give evidence, the Rules require that you make the solemn declaration. The text is now handed out to you. May I invite to you make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated, Mr. Mladjenovic. Mr. Mladjenovic, you will first examined by Mr. Stojanovic. You will find him to your left. Mr. Stojanovic is counsel for Mr. Mladic. Mr. Stojanovic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning once again. Good morning, Mr. Mladjenovic.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please state your full name slowly for the record.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Radojica Mladjenovic, son of Rado and Dunja, born in Metrevac, Foca municipality on the 20th of November, 1949.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Mladjenovic, will you please tell the Chamber if you have given a statement, a written statement to the Defence team of General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we please call up 1D01654, 65 ter.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mladjenovic, you can see in front of you the cover page of a statement, and I'm asking you is this your signature?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: That is correct, it's my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can we now please look at the last page of this document. And, Mr. Mladjenovic, the same question: The signature that you see on that page, is that your signature, and did you enter this date?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Mladjenovic, during proofing for your today's appearance before this Court, we established that a couple of things need to be clarified or, rather, amend your statement for better understanding.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: That is correct. My opinion was that in order not to waste time, this should be defined in more accurate terms but style-wise, the essence would remain the same, and that relates to a few paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Since, for the record, we have to go through these issues, I'd kindly ask you to look at paragraph 2 of your statement, which you have in front of you, and you will have a hard copy in a short while. You indicated that in the last sentence, something has to be added precisely the words after the words, "He was the only Serb, to read the first on the election ticket ..." so that finally this sentence should read --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Stojanovic please indicate where he is reading from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, you're invited to indicate where you're reading from.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, Your Honours, I'm reading paragraph 2 of this witness's statement, the last sentence. May I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mladjenovic, can we now look at paragraph 5 of your statement where you pointed out --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Before you continue, the sentence you wanted to read, the last sentence in paragraph 2, in the new version was not recorded. If you want to have that on the record, you should read that again.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. [Interpretation] Yes, thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So the sentence, the final sentence in paragraph 2, last sentence, should read as follows: "This means that I was the only Serb who was on the top of the ticket among the five parties on the eve of the 1990 elections." Thank you. Now, in paragraph 5, Mr. Mladjenovic, in the second sentence, after the word "the division of the SDS and the SDA," the following should be added: "Other political parties did not have much say," and then the remaining of the text remains the same. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is. Because we constituted an absolute majority.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now is it appropriate for me to read the entire sentence?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Please go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: It reads now: "In the division between the SDS and the SDA, other political parties did not have much say. At one point these two parties reached an agreement so that the TO went to the SDS through the position of chief, i.e., Sulejman Pilav who held this position until the last day and equally to the Serbs, Muslims and Croats, whereas the military department went to the SDA." Is that now a correct statement?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can we now focus on paragraph 11?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I can't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Please wait for a second. Where you --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can we enlarge it a bit? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Where you indicated that something needs to be clarified, precisely the second sentence, so that it should read as follows: "When the assembly was established on recommendation as the population of Foca was Muslim by a slim majority, the president," and then this should be added: Of the Serbian Crisis Staff was supposed to be the president of the Foca SDS. And then: "Petko Cancar, a lawyer, was the first president. I, Radojica Mladjenovic, vice-president, and Miroslav Stanic, the secretary of the party. "Following the election of Mr. Cancar to the National Assembly of BH, and my appointment as president of the executive committee of Foca municipality, Miroslav Stanic became president of the SDS, so that in addition to Miroslav Stanic, the following also became members thereof: Josip Milicic as president of the Serbian municipality, I myself as the president of the executive committee, and other members." Would this be the clarification that is sufficient for you to stand by what has been recorded?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: The essence is absolutely correct. I think that the Tribunal knows that the Crisis Staff was made up of 15 members, so apart from the ones named here, there were others as well, and that was published in the gazette of Foca municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now look at paragraph 14. Here, you felt the need to explain the second sentence, which now should read as follows: "Gentlemen Varajic and Dzemo Aganovic came to the municipality, and I gave them handwritten notes of 16 points that should have been agreed to by the Muslim side. Also agreed was to terminate any armed clashes. "Varajic made a cursory glance of the request of the Serbian side and all that he said was as follows: 'You shouldn't have called me at all.' "At that point in time, there were already sounds of shelling from the Muslim positions, precisely from the Sukovac direction, which was followed by a Serbian response from the eastern part of the town beneath Zabrana." Now having made this amendment, is this text now consistent with what you remember?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: This is authentic and this is a truthful interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: That's why I wanted this to -- to -- made more specific in order for us to save some time for discussion.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And let me just draw your attention to another correction, in paragraph 18. Let's have a look at it. I'm talking about the last sentence. It reads as follows: In inverted commas -- I'm sorry. Thank you. And I quote: "According more to the records of the Red Cross about 3.000." Now this is just a semantic correction so it should read as follows: "According to the Red Cross records, more than 3.000 people."

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: We are talking about the Red Cross. According to the Red Cross records?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, after we have made these corrections and provided these clarifications as per your request, Mr. Mladjenovic, let me ask you this:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, before you ask this, I just want to get a clarification. You said CK was now clarified. This is the Red Cross. But you changed one word as well. In the original, it says: About 3.000 of them left. Now you said more than 3.000 left. Could you clarify with the witness what his position is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will do so, Your Honours. We are looking at the B/C/S version which creates a problem, but I will ask him anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mladjenovic, can you please look again at paragraph 18. In the original text, have you ever mentioned that the figure was the one that exceeded 3.000?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Ladies and gentlemen, these figures varied every month or every week tremendously. In this first wave this figure was recorded by the Foca and Pluzine Red Cross organisation and it was approximately 3.000.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. "Approximately." That's translated into "about" in the original statement, it is not more than 3.000. I just wanted to clarify what is the correct term in the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This now being clarified, please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Mladjenovic, having provided these clarifications to your statement and after you have given a solemn declaration in this courtroom that you will speak, to the best of your knowledge and recollection, the truth and nothing but the truth, do you fully stand by the statement as it is now in writing before you?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do, and I accept it as mine. Given to this Court, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we please tender the statement of Witness Radojica Mladjenovic, 65 ter 1D01654, into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D1654 receives number D697, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your leave, Your Honours, I'm going to read the summary of this witness's statement and then I will have a few questions for him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Proceed as you suggest, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After the first multi-party elections in 1990, the witness, Radojica Mladjenovic, as the first person on the SDS ticket at the first multi-party elections in BiH in 1990, was elected president of the Foca municipality executive committee and remained in that position until the end of the war. He directly participated in the negotiations surrounding the establishment of authorities and division of departments in the municipality of Foca. He will discuss the different views concerning the positions that were supposed to be divided between SDS and SDA cadres, the interethnic problems caused by a clash at Focatrans and the growing interethnic tensions. Just before the war broke out in Foca, on the 8th of April, 1992, he participated in an attempt to peacefully divide power. It failed totally, although both sides to the negotiations signed a document on how to divide power locally. On the same day, already in the afternoon, the Muslim side reneged on the agreement it had signed. Fighting intensified. The witness knows that the Muslim side launched an attack on a church using makeshift mortars or a launcher. It led to fighting in the town that lasted for several days. By late July 1992, the Serb side managed to gain control over most of the territory of the municipality of Foca. The witness is personally aware that the Muslims left Foca without being expelled in any way. They followed their leadership, which fled, having previously realised that they would be defeated militarily. He testifies that there is no way that a plan or order for the Muslims to leave Foca existed. They went in the direction of Gorazde on buses or in cars. Finally, the witness will discuss General Mladic's position on paramilitary formations, and he states that he was aware that the KP Dom in Foca was under the authority of the Ministry of Justice of Republika Srpska, and that the appointment of Krnojelac as warden of the KP Dom Foca was motivated by the fact that he was a competent teacher and captain first class. With your leave, Your Honours, I'd like to put a few questions to the witness now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mladjenovic, D697, paragraph 3, paragraph 3, you speak about the efforts made after the multi-party elections in Foca in 1990 to have the results of the elections implemented and to share power in the municipality. Were agreements reached in terms of how power would be shared and how the government would function?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: The SDA and the SDS reached agreements to that effect, to resolve all personnel issues, and they proceeded with great difficulty. At the meeting of the assembly on the 25th of December, 1990 - how do I put this? - it was smooth sailing for the late Mr. Lojo and myself, that is to say that they were officially elected already. After that, there was a lot of unexpected things that happened. Things had agreed -- been agreed upon but not implemented until the conflict broke out on the 8th of April, 1992; for example, the TO and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have 65 ter 1D04509 in e-court, please. Could we please take a look at the second page now and then we'll go back to the beginning of the text. In B/C/S, could we have a look at the second page now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mladjenovic, in the lower left-hand corner, is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. My signature and Taib's signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please go back to the beginning, to the first page in B/C/S. According to this protocol dated the 4th of March, 1992, on behalf of the SDS, as stated here, you reached an agreement with the SDA that was then headed by -- or, rather, Taib Lojo was a participant in these talks. Was this agreement implemented in reality?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: No, it was not. Because practically there wasn't enough time. So the 4th of April -- actually, the 4th of March. Well, it could have been but this was not completed. I think that only the deputy prosecutor was appointed in court or some of the other persons who were candidates. As for all these other matters, all of that was not carried through. So until the 8th of April, Mr. Sulejman Pilav was head of the joint TO and already promulgated head of the Crisis Staff of the SDA so he had a dual role, as it were.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: At that time, do you have any knowledge about the arming of citizens in the municipality of Foca?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, since I'm testifying under oath, there were different rumours that went around town about the arming of Serbs and Muslims and the ways in which this arming was being carried out, either by opening this notorious Focatrans line, that is to say, a bus between Istanbul and Foca, and Split and Foca purportedly for purposes of tourism. So this mess developed in Focatrans and contributed to a feeling of hatred among the two peoples and even Montenegrins, because there were quite a few of them in these companies as well or, rather, this company, Focatrans. That's what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could document 65 ter 1D04509 be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D4509 receives number D698, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In paragraph 13 -- could we have document D697 in e-court again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You speak about a meeting held on the 8th of April, 1992. Paragraph 13. Could you please tell the Court where this meeting was held physically between the most responsible representatives of the Serb and Muslim sides in Foca?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please show it from the very beginning. Which paper is that? Is that the one that we needed to have signed?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Look at paragraph 13.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: 13? All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You say a meeting was held on the 8th of April, 1992. Now this is what I'm asking you.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Oh, yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you tell the Court where the meeting was held physically?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: The meeting was held in my office and the initiative was of the late Mr. Taib Lojo as president of the Assembly, and he was practically the president of the National Defence Council ex officio. It was attended by all members of the executive committee that were elected to that position by the assembly. I remember all five of them and I was the sixth one and there was Taib Lojo and my secretary who was taking notes, taking down the minutes. If I need to provide the name -- names.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No, not really.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: They were legally and legitimately elected at the joint session of the assembly. I mean, Serbs and Muslims together, certainly. And on that day, practically, irrespective of all these variants --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I think the question is answered with the first sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Yes, that's right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What was the purpose of that meeting, Mr. Mladjenovic?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: The purpose of this meeting was at least a last-ditch attempt, since there were so many discussions, and especially I and Mr. Taib at the time, to find any solution just in order to prevent a war. We were even prepared to divide the territory on the basis of reciprocity so no one would move from their land. The essence was that the Muslim -- that the local communes or villages, rather, where the population was predominantly Muslim, or Bosniak, if you will, that that territory should be annexed to the territory of the Muslim part, although there were some Serb families there. And the other way around.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, please, I have to stop you here. Tell us, how long did this meeting last, to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I think it started about 8.00. It lasted, say, an hour, an hour and a half, and then there was this cannonade or explosion. Under the hill of Celovine, there's the KP Dom. And at that time, the KP Dom people were released. I really don't know who released them, so it was Serbs and Muslims all of them were released. Murderers included. And then they started running towards that hill and reached the forest. And then this explosion went off. I was facing that area with my back. We all jumped to our feet. And then panic prevailed. We started thinking about what to do, and then later on there was a curfew that was imposed and so on and so forth and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Once the witness has answered your question - he did after the first two lines - then you can put your next question to the witness, Mr. Stojanovic. Apart from whether it would change either the Prosecution's or the Defence case considerably if the meeting had lasted three hours or half an hour. I mean, relevance of the length of that meeting is uncertain.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: At one moment, did you conclude an agreement, nevertheless, as negotiators on that day?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The secretary of the municipality, who was a Muslim, was making things a bit difficult. But, as you can see, on the basis of these signatures, an agreement was reached. I have the original with different pens, pencils, et cetera, but it is an authentic document and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes was the answer to your question. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. D582. Could we please have that document in e-court now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mladjenovic, is this the text of the agreement that you signed together on that day on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: The text or, rather, the content of the text, is comprehensive and correct. However, at least in this variant that you're showing me, there is something missing. You can only see part of my signature and Taib's signature can be seen. However, there are five or six signatures. I have the original. All the participants of the meeting were given a copy of their own so we were standing there and I was writing in my notebook who was supposed to do what, what the Crisis Staff was supposed to, and the police that was then called milicija, then we, I and Mr. Taib what we were supposed to. Are we supposed to impose a curfew through the media, or are we supposed to introduce a state of emergency or emergency measures. I believe that that is the last point.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell us, on the original document, can we find your signature and the signature of Taib Lojo?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, and five other persons, Muslims and Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, and I'm going to conclude with this question: Who was it that caused the non-implementation of this agreement and the outbreak of hostilities in Foca?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: It was my profound hope that we would work towards a solution on the basis of these points. You can see here who was in charge of what, the KP Dom, et cetera. However, the members of the executive committee, Mr. Varajic, my school friend, and Mr. Varajic to hand over to them the request of the Crisis Staff that was dictated by Minister Ostojic, actually, we were still in the municipality, already there was gun-fire and we parted, we went in different ways and --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The question was -- the question was, according to you, who was responsible for the failure of the implementation of this agreement and who started the conflict in Foca?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Obviously the Muslim side. Because they were first to start shooting, and, secondly, they never came with an affirmative answer that they accepted it. So, actually, we were never told whether they accepted it or rejected it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mladjenovic. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stojanovic. Ms. Bibles, are you ready to start your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladjenovic, you will now be cross-examined by Ms. Bibles. You will find her to your right. Ms. Bibles is counsel for the Prosecution. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning to you too.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to start by going through your evidence chronologically. Will you confirm that the Serbian municipality of Foca was formed on the 21st of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: The Serbian municipality of Foca was formed, I think, on the 25th of December, 1991. Following the model that was implemented at the republican level after the separation and outvoting and so on and so forth. And I'm talking about the BH assembly.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, in paragraph 10 of your statement, your Mladic statement, you describe the creation of the Assembly of the Serbian People. Just to be clear, are we talking about or are you describing the assembly in Foca? Just very simply that question.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please -- is it something on -- on paper?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I believe Mr. --

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know which context you're asking me about General Mladic because he wasn't there. He was not present either in the army --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... witness, let me stop you there. Ms. Bibles referred to the statement you've given, and I see that you're reading the transcript. If you listen to the interpretation in your own language, that may avoid confusions like the one we just heard about. Could you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, I'd ask you because of your reading of the transcript, do you speak or read English?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: No, unfortunately not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I was mistaken when I thought that the witness was reading the transcript, whereas he is apparently reading on what appears on e-court. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, what I asked, simply, is, in your statement for this trial, you describe the creation of the Assembly of the Serbian People. Are you describing the assembly -- in that paragraph, are you describing the assembly in Foca?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. And representatives of who were legitimately elected of the socialist party became deputies as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I was simply looking, wanting to clarify that you were talking about the assembly in Foca. Now in paragraph 10 where you talk about this process, you explained further that this was: "Following this model without any specific initiative from a higher level, there ensued the setting up of organs 'just in case'." Sir I want to ask some questions about this section of your statement. Before I do that, I want to confirm, did you attend the extended session of the Social Democratic Party Main Board and executive committee which was held in Sarajevo on 14 February 1992?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I'd like to play an audio clip of a statement that we believe you made to this body. I'll ask that we play just from the beginning to, I believe, it's a minute, 26. For the booths, the English translation this would begin at the beginning of the transcript and it goes to the second page at line 6. In B/C/S, it's from the bottom of the page, the first page, to 14 lines down in the second page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would playing it once be sufficient, Ms. Bibles, or should it be played twice in order to allow our interpreters to verify whether the transcript reflect what is heard in the audio?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the counsel give us the number of the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I forgot to give the 65 ter number, which is 10925A. And I understand that we will need to play this twice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then let's play it now for the first time. The interpreters have found the document. Yes. Let's get started.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It went on until 1 minute, 29:3. Witness, we'll play it again. You'll hear it again. The Chamber will now receive interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "Radojica Mladjenovic: I am speaking on behalf of the Serbian Executive Committee of Foca municipality and that other one that is slowly dying. I do not wish to participate in the debate here, but I would like to ask some questions that I would like to find answers to, that is, I, as a representative of the people in Foca municipality, Serbian people of Foca municipality, considering the fact that we did everything that the central office had requested us to do, and considering the instructions we received in this field when setting up the Serbian Assembly and Executive Committee. We got far ahead with the work of the Executive Committee for a simple reason, at least with some operational issues by which we wish to finally round up the Serbian territory of Foca municipality within the Serbian Autonomous Region of Herzegovina. Of course, we wouldn't think of resolving the Serbian territory in Bosnia and Herzegovina partially. For these reasons, I find it necessary to, first of all, establish Serbian municipalities regardless of the borders of existing municipalities, that is the case with us, and we will not have any regard for that. In the same manner ..."

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, do you accept that this is your voice speaking on the 14th of February, 1992?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, in this 1992 audio recording, we've heard you say that in setting up the Serbian Assembly and the Executive Committee in Foca that you did everything that the central office requested, according to the instructions. Do you agree that these were the instructions which were received from the Main Board of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: As far as the instructions allegedly from the central office are concerned, but they are mentioned here, all of this pertained to Foca municipality, and the structure which, by inertia, simply mimicked the happenings at the republican level, so applied the same analogy. Which is to say on 25th of December, 1992, we set up our assembly, as I said, just in case, the people of Foca, both Muslims and Serbs --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps the witness could end that sentence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They had some very bad experiences in the past so that everybody was afraid of everybody. In view of the First World War, the Second World War --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, just answer the question. The question was whether these were instructions that you received from the Main Board of the SDS. Now you started your answer, by saying: "As far as the instructions allegedly from the central office," who alleged that? Isn't it that you yourself did so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Central office" can be interpreted in different ways, and in different situations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you use those words?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I finish, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, you may not. You may -- did you use those words?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I did. That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Next question, please, Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, the Chamber has received evidence that just days before the Foca Assembly was established, that the Main Board of the SDS issued detailed instructions that Serb assemblies should be created. The Prosecution theory in this case is that the setting up of separate Serbian municipal organs in Foca occurred as a direct result of a plan from the Bosnian Serb leadership that was applied all over Bosnia. The contradiction between your written statement for this trial in 2014 and your words spoken in 1992 make it appear that you are trying to hide this overarching plan for the creation of the Serbian state in Bosnia and Herzegovina. What do you say to that?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: If you were listening carefully, in one segment, it says that no setting up should be contrary to what was happening all over Bosnia-Herzegovina and in order to make it even clearer, all the efforts that were made, and I must say that, the municipality assembly of Foca never became operational prior to the 8th of April, 1994. Not even the Executive Committee which was established on the 3rd of April. So this absolutely cannot be consistent with this proposition. In other words, nobody was making any preparations, and according to the information that we have from JNA organs relating to the army and the similar things, the Muslims and the Croats had a huge advantage because the Serbs believed that Bosnia-Herzegovina will remain in Yugoslavia and that we shall have only one army which will contribute to solving the problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It looks as if you're moving away from the question. What Ms. Bibles puts to you, and I'll try to say it short --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no other intention other than to provide clarification. That's all I wish to do. I don't want to deviate from the subject.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bibles puts to you that in your statement you say it was all our own initiative; whereas, in the audio you are saying that you did everything that the central office had requested you to do and that you acted upon instructions you received in this field when setting up the Serbian Assembly and Executive Committee. Ms. Bibles apparently sees some contradiction in what you state and what she heard in the audio and is asking a comment on that specifically, the contradiction between the two: Own initiative, or following instructions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Concerning the instructions, given that we had representatives in the republican authorities and one of them was Mr. Maksimovic, the chairman of the Deputies Club, we used this information in order to copy, so to say, what was happening at the republican level. In other words, in the National Assembly of Serbs in BH as it was originally called, just so that in a case of certain situations occurring, we would be prepared, sort of. That's all. The other subject discussed was the sloppiness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me interrupt you again. It seems that Ms. Bibles is not talking about following an example and a national Assembly of Serbs in BH but she's talking about instructions given by the SDS Main Board. So apparently you are talking at cross-purposes. Whether or not you received and followed instructions, as you said, by the central office; and I understand Ms. Bibles to understand your statement as referring to the SDS Main Board and not to the National Assembly of Serbs in BH. Could you please focus on that. Ms. Bibles, if I understood you well.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If it is necessary, I can repeat, that I emphasise that all of this relates only to Foca municipality. If you wish, you can hear the audio once again, and you can hear that it relates to Foca. Anyway, the Dayton Accords divided the municipality of Foca into two parts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No one is claiming that it is not about Foca. You're speaking about having followed all the instructions, and we understand that to be in the Foca context. The issue is in your statement you say it was not without any specific initiative from a higher level, whereas Ms. Bibles puts to you that -- in your audio you say that you implemented all the instructions you received, which means that there was an initiative from the higher level because there were instructions. That's the issue; nothing else.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand what you're saying, absolutely. I think that contacts with the central office, according to the hierarchy, were few and far between, and it happened only when it was really necessary between myself - not only myself, I'm not trying to justify what I did - but also with all the people who were at the core of all the events and who were, at the same time, representatives of Foca, whether as deputies or in other bodies. So these contacts may, ultimately, be considered to be something that was sent in form of recommendations from the central office rather than orders, because there were no orders whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Had you received any instructions from the central office in setting up the Serbian organs in Foca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No instructions were received for the setting up of organs. We only followed the model that was in place following the walking out of the assembly of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Serbs on one side and Muslims and Croats on both sides, and the dates can be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have any explanation as why you said in this speech: "And considering the instructions we received in this field," because you're now saying you didn't receive any instructions, that needs an explanation, why you said that you did receive and why you now say you did not receive instructions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Probably in plural, because, as I already said, there were various sources, including the deputies in the assembly, the president of the Deputies Club. So I used the plural. I, myself, did not directly receive any guidance as to the setting up of this -- these organs because there was no government formed at the level of the Serbian Bosnia-Herzegovina assembly only. Later on, we elected new members to the Executive Committee once we went our separate ways with other members of the administration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If that's your explanation, I'll invite Ms. Bibles to put her next question to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And, actually, I'm looking at the clock. I believe it might be time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it's time for a break. Witness, we'd like to see you back in 20 minutes from now. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I may be able to use the few seconds here. I would tender 65 ter 10925A, which was the audio recording.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 10925A receives number P6834, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6834 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And to speed the next two questions, we could also go to P3038, and we'll stay on page 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, there's a document coming up on the screen, P3038 which I'd like to you look at. I'm going to show you two pages on this document and then I'm going to ask you one question. The document that we see in front of us indicates that it is from the SDS Main Board. It is titled: "Instructions for the organisation and operation of organs of the Serbian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina in emergency conditions," and it's dated 19 December 1991. Now, if we could turn to pages 7 in both English and B/C/S, and we'll be focussing on point 4, please. Sir, you'll see in point 4 of this page that, in part, the instructions direct to: "Convene and proclaim an assembly of the Serbian people in the municipality composed of assemblymen, representatives of the Serbian people in the municipal assembly and presidents of SDS local boards." And I'll stop reading there. But, sir, isn't it true -- is it true that this is exactly what occurred in Foca on the 25th of December in 1991?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: It is correct the assembly was convened by the president of the municipal SDS board, the late Miro Stanic, who was the president of the party at the time, and that is when the assembly was formed, composed of all Serbian Assemblymen who were members of the reformist party, the Communist party, and the SDS, and it also included members or, rather, presidents of SDS local boards in villages and towns, some 20-odd of them, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, we're not going to go point by point through every aspect of this instruction. Wouldn't you agree -- or don't you agree that it's very clear that what was happening in Foca was exactly what was described in these instructions?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: As for the knowledge about this initiative, was something that was conveyed to the president of the party. If he did receive any, any way he should have received some kind of instruction as how to act in Foca municipality, because you can see for yourself, that this relates to hem.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, it's true, isn't it, that the organisation which began to occur in December of 1991 in Foca was according to these instructions which it appears were given out to Serbian people all over Bosnia. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: It turns out that that could be true.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll move on now from this document and quickly go through just a couple of other areas, sir. First, you were elected as chairman of the Executive Committee of the Assembly of Serbian People in Foca; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And then move -- sir, moving forward in time, on 3 April 1992, the Assembly of the Serbian Municipality of Foca established the Foca Crisis Staff; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: That is correct. The 3rd and the 4th -- actually, the 3rd of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And if we could now have 65 ter 8611B on our screens, we'll be looking at page 2 in the original and page 3 in the English. Sir, the document that will be coming up on our screen is a section of the Official Gazette of the Serbian municipality of Foca. We'll see a list of people beginning with Miroslav Stanic. We'll wait for that list to come up. While we're doing that -- oops. It appears the list is there on the B/C/S, or ...

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... now second on the list --

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Second on the list is the president of the party and the president of the municipality, I believe it is Josef Milicic; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: The second one, yes. I'm the third one and so on. Until number 15.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And can you --

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: It was on the basis of the office held.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, can you confirm that the list of individuals here comprised the Crisis Staff in Foca?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Not Foca. Rather, the Serb part of the people of Foca, if I can put it that way, because the Muslims also had their Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you for that clarification.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And with that, Your Honour, I move to tender 65 ter 8611B which would be the entire section on the Crisis Staff formation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 8611B receives number P6835, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Now, sir, earlier today - I believe on temporary transcript page 16 - you indicated that Velibor Ostojic was present in Foca on the 8th of April, 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I think so. I think - how do I put this? - I think he was the Crisis Staff -- on the premises of the Crisis Staff but that is not exactly likely either. I think he was in one of the family homes there, because he seemed very scared. I don't know how to put this. But he came and he dictated these 16 points, and I handed them over to Mr. Varajic and Dzemo Aganovic. Later on, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And, sir, is it correct that in addition to being the Republika Srpska minister of information, Ostojic was also, at that time, the state commissioner for Foca municipality?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: At one point in time, he was the first commissioner, actually. And then later on there was a change, Vojislav Maksimovic, and then he didn't turn out to be the right solution. And then MP Mijetovic from Trebinje was in that position.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Now, sir, you were on the Crisis Staff. You were also president of the Executive Committee, so you had a leadership role in Foca. Would you agree that, as such, you were a person in Foca municipality who made efforts to find out what was going on in Foca in April and May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: You're not right on each and every point. I wish you were. Because already in May, many things looked different. Units that nobody invited are coming, and obviously the motives are looting and something else. I, or, rather, Foca as a town -- I mean --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, I need to apologise. I don't think I asked a precise question and perhaps I can go forward in a way that will make more sense. In paragraph 15 of your statement, you discuss things like finding out about the release of prisoners from KP Dom, and you describe at some point there was fighting around the health centre. Now, you explain - and that's what I want to clarify - it appears that you explain that you were aware of this because you were listening to information from ham radio operators. First, is that correct? Is that a part of how you were receiving information?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I want to tell the truth. No one had invited them, these paramilitaries --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: -- about 70 men --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, listen to the question, answer the question. Ms. Bibles will define what she'd like to hear from you. Therefore, did you receive that information by listening to -- or least partly by listening to the ham radio operators?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ham radio operators, or Radio Sarajevo, if that's what you mean. 5.000 Chetniks arriving in Foca, that's the statement made by Radio Sarajevo. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm going to stop you now. If you want this Chamber to include your evidence when we are considering this case, then you're advised to answer the questions. No one asked you what was broadcasted. What was asked was whether you received information through the means of listening to those radio operators. Did you, or did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, but if ham radio operators are considered to be radio information I mean, I think that that was the question and that is what the lady was getting at. So ham radio operators and I mean, in my statement I -- well, I allow for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Not what you allow for, but did you receive information by listening to this radio broadcast of -- ham radio operators?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you. I now want to shift gears and just confirm -- actually, if we could go to P2820.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, this is a Belgrade Radio report regarding events in Foca. It's a report given by Velibor Ostojic. You've confirmed that Ostojic was in Foca municipality on the 8th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: You -- can you confirm, then, that he was reporting to the outside world what was going -- the events in Foca on the 8th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: That I don't know, and I wasn't present. As for this text -- oh, all right.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: That's all. Moving on now to P2824, sir, this is a report from Ostojic - it will be coming up on your screen - dated 30 April 1992. I see the B/C/S version has come up. You'll see that Ostojic reports that Foca Serbian TO liberated the area of Ustikolina he also reported that the Serb TO in Foca was making efforts in the rest of the area to clean up - or he uses the word "ciscenje" - Foca. Can you tell us - simple yes or no - whether you know if Ostojic was in Foca on the 30th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember the 30th. Just may I explain this, please, I came to the municipality as the civilian representative or rather I informed or rather activated the work of the Executive Council on the 19th. Now the 30th, I don't think so, because he himself admitted that he felt that he bothered us and he went to Pale, I think. When, I cannot say, really, believe me.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: So let's -- let's slow this down just a little bit. If I understand your testimony correctly, Ostojic if I'm understanding it right on the 19th, or in this time-period, expressed that he felt like he was bothering you. Now, by "bothering us," I think is the phrase you used, does that mean the authorities in Foca municipality?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Bothering us. Well, he said it himself.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: All right. So after that, Ostojic went back to Pale; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: To Pale, because the government was supposed to be established and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: So let's go back now to the document on the screen. Can you confirm that the events that he describes in this report are accurate?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. April? I'm not sure. I'm not sure that that is accurate enough or, rather, that it is accurate. Or it's a half-truth. Because in Ustikolina in these village, there were Muslim forces present as well. So it's not reliable, as far as I'm concerned.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: We'll move on then. And I do want to talk about some of the forces. And we can take this from the screen. In terms of Serb forces that were part of what I believe you refer to as the liberation of Foca, I just want to ask you a very few limited questions about a group of 60 men that were referred to as the Belgrade battalion. You agree that this group was led by a man whose last name was Lainovic?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. There's some confusion there. The Belgrade group or, rather, the people who lived in Belgrade but who originally came from Celebici, Zejt [phoen], Mestrovac, these villages, they came as volunteers and they withdrew on the day when the JNA withdrew. As for Lainovic is concerned, that is that special group that created such a mess in Foca that it spilled over throughout Herzegovina almost because their motto was basically just to loot and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, was there a group known under the name as Belgrade battalion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, we called them the Belgrade battalion because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So was that a group of approximately 60 men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Approximately 60 men. All of them originally from that area --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I'm not asking where they came from. I asked you about the size. Approximately 60 men. By whom were they led? What person was leading them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Bodiroga. I'm not sure of his first name. An elderly man. They wore uniforms and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not asking you what they were wearing I asked you who was leading them. Did Mr. Lainovic have anything to do with this group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Bodiroga. No he had an independent group.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You've answered the questions. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Can you confirm that the Belgrade battalion participated in events in Foca relating to the liberation of Foca but withdrew in the middle of May 1992?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: This so-called Belgrade battalion came after the 15th of April. After the 15th of April. And a large part of that unit was securing the hospital that is, say, 2 or 3 kilometres away from the separation line. Downstream towards Gorazde, if you look at the Drina River.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Is it true that they left Foca or they withdrew from Foca in the middle --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bibles, could we please have an answer to the previous question. Did they participate in the events in Foca relating to the liberation? Or should we understand your answer to be that securing the hospital was part of that operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct. But after that, they were involved or they were subordinated, in military terms, to the Territorial Defence Staff, the Serb units, that is, up until that date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say after that. Beginning on what date exactly were they subordinated to the TO Defence Staff? If you don't know, tell us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I cannot say specifically or precisely whether they withdrew on the 15th of May, around the 15th of May, and then they arrived on the 15th of April. Believe me, I cannot engage in guess-work --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We did not understand the last part of the sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What did you say after you said: "I cannot engage in guess-work" because the interpreters didn't catch the last portion of your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I cannot state with certainty when it was that they joined the TO units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, perhaps it would be helpful for us to bring up a section of your testimony when you testified here in the Karadzic case.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could go to 65 ter 31459.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And, sir, there is your testimony from the 5th of April, 2013.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could go to page 31.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, we do not have this transcript in B/C/S so you don't need to look at the screen. I will try to read the relevant portions of this to you. See if this assists you. Starting at line 4, you were asked a question: "Mr. Mladjenovic, we were just coming onto discuss the Serb forces that remained in Foca area after the JNA withdrawal. "Now, the civilian authorities in Foca closely liaised with the military authorities in pursuit of their shared goals, didn't they?" Your answer was this: "I have to correct you straight away. Military formations and paramilitaries that appeared at the very beginning of the war in Foca - on the 15th of May, the Army of Republika Srpska was ... set up, and they withdrew. It was not a battalion. There were some 60 men or so. That's what we called them, because the locals who hailed from Belgrade and Foca - and, for that reason, that's what we called them." Sir, do you stand by your testimony with respect to the -- the withdrawal of these units on the 15th of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, they withdrew on the 15th, or, at the latest, when the JNA had to withdraw.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: But I think it was on the 15th, though.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Is it also true that after 12 May 1992, when the VRS was created, that the military situation for Serbian Foca was more organised and improved?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: The situation improved only after the 28th of June, 1992, when the brigade was formed. The Foca Light Brigade, if I'm not mistaken. And from then onwards, there was this organised military structure. After that, came the tactical group and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Now, sir, thank you. Thank you. And I ... I want to direct your attention to the 16th Assembly of the RS which occurred on 12 May 1992 in Banja Luka. Were you present for that assembly?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: No, because I wasn't a Member of Parliament now.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Do you know who represented Foca in the assembly?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I think I do know. Of course, if they went or if they could have gone, it should have been Vojislav Maksimovic and Petko Cancar. They were the MPs from the ranks of the Serb people.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: When did you hear that Ratko Mladic was the head of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I think that I heard that a day or two later, after the decision was made at this same assembly that the Army of Republika Srpska should be established.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I want to turn now to some interactions between the Crisis Staff in Foca and the Executive Committee in Foca between those two organs and the republic-level government after 12 May 1992?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could have 65 ter 15977, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, this is a request from the Republika Srpska government directed to the Foca Crisis Staff. As this document is coming up, I'll ask if you know who Veljko Kostovic is? And I see that you're looking at the B/C/S documents. We see --

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Veljko?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I apologise. My pronunciation may have been off.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I mean, the signature -- oh yes, Veljko Kostovic I know him. He was director of the Official Gazette of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And, sir, we see that this is actually a document dated 23 May 1992, stamped from the RS Bosnia-Herzegovina government and it's requesting that gentleman to be the editor of the Official Gazette of the Serbian People in Bosnia-Herzegovina. So based on your response, you'll confirm that this request from the RS government to the Crisis Staff was granted?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We did not hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In all frankness, I don't think that this got through the Crisis Staff. Because Mr. Kostovic at the time was staying in the village of ... near the village of Borovnici that's perhaps a kilometre away. In a family home.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: -- but down this military line he probably received information and --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: This document is addressed to the Crisis Staff Foca, not to Mr. Kostovic. So it would have been received by the Crisis Staff Foca and the Crisis Staff Foca would communicate with Mr. Kostovic the request contained here. Isn't it so? I see you're nodding. Can you just say in words what you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Quite possibly. Quite possibly. I was a member of the Crisis Staff, but already from the 19th of April, that is to say --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: All I wanted to know this is document is addressed to the Crisis Staff. I'm not asking you about your membership. Yes, thank you, Madam Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: -- at temporary page 38, you described this individual is -- was director of the Official Gazette of Republika Srpska. I was inferring that that meant that this request was granted by the Foca Crisis Staff; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Until after the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And I would tender --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not an answer to the question. And --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very probably.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course, the two are not the same, Ms. Bibles. Him finally becoming or having that position doesn't mean that he went with the permission of the Crisis Staff. He could have gone there otherwise but that's let's leave it. You confirm that he took up that position and stayed in that position until the end of the war. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And I would tender 15977.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. Until 2000, roughly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 15977 receives number P6836, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Now, sir, I want to look at an example of the Foca local authority -- Serbian local authorities reaching out to the republic level.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could see P2822 on our screens, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, this is a document signed by Miroslav Stanic on 18 June -- or the document that's coming up. On 18 June 1992 regarding decisions to allow Muslims to leave Foca municipality. If you see the number 1 about halfway down the page, the line I want to look at is just above that where it reads: "The War Commission has discussed the issue with the government envoy in the [sic] Bosnia-Herzegovina Serbian republic and concluded the following... " Who was the envoy?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment let me look at the date. I think that was Professor Dr. Vojislav Maksimovic. I am quite certain, because I think he was there at the time. Yes, yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And I'd next like to look at number 5 which will require turning to page 2 in the B/C/S version. Sir I'd like you to direct your attention to number 5 in the document. This describes that the Executive Committee would draw up a list of property that would remain in Foca, meaning that it couldn't leave Foca. Was this property that belonged to Muslims who were leaving?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Absolutely not. Because the Executive Committee formulated the protection of property of both Muslims and Serbs in a different ways. Quite a few Serbs left either for Belgrade or for Montenegro, so this encompasses both their property, houses and flats. I don't know what he meant when he spoke about businesses and companies. I don't think that is relevant.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: So, sir, you were on the Executive Committee; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Was this list drawn up?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember that. Let me just briefly take a look. To tell you the truth, I'm not familiar with this document. Even though it assigned some tasks to the Executive Committee, but I don't remember seeing this piece of paper.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Now, sir, when we first looked at this document and I asked you whether this was property belonging to Muslims, you had an answer with respect to property which was Serb -- if I understand it correctly, was Serbian houses and flats. Am I understanding that right, in terms of the property that this would be referring to?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: The Executive Committee issued an order or, rather, proposed an order to be issued by the army and the police to print some instructions to the effect that all the flats and houses that had been abandoned, of course, not forever, to be sealed off, that this should be monitored by the civilian police and they acted accordingly. Even the process itself started but during a chaotic period of time in Foca, after which I had to intervene with government, seeking assistance to resolve the situation. This whole process was suspended. I believe that there is a form stipulating all the rules as to who was going to monitor this, including the military police and the civilian police.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I seek clarification of one of the previous answers.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said that: "Because the Executive Committee formulated," and now it disappears from my screen. One second, please. You said: "Because the Executive Committee formulated the protection of property of both Muslims and Serbs in a different ways," that's unclear to me. Could you explain in what way the protection of property of Muslims and Serbs was different?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, you absolutely misunderstood me. This same piece of paper was to be posted on the front door of both Serbs and Muslims' flats who abandoned them. And that was something that the civilian police, or milicija, and the military police were charged with monitoring the process, because at the beginning of war, a large number of Serbs left the area via Pluzine or in some other manner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: You've described this property, if I'm understanding it be correctly, to be Serb homes or flats. Now, number 5, this indicates that the Executive Committee is to draw up a list of property that will remain in Foca, meaning property that cannot be transported under any circumstances. What kinds of property -- that does not sound like flats or houses. So what kind of property is this describing?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, and I think I did, in both Muslim and Serb shops, there was some intermediate material that happened to be there. The Executive Committee set up a commission - you can find all the documents - to arrange for the evacuation of some of the equipment and in order for do that, the walls had to be torn down and they were all put in central store house. Roof tiles, met tall sheet, et cetera. All these records still exist to this very day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Ms. Bibles, I think there is a reason for misinterpretation. You said and referring to paragraph 5, "property that cannot be transported under any circumstances," but I read "under current circumstances." I think this is really different. You should clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I also had some clarification to ask from you, Madam Bibles you said what kinds of property this is - page 44, line 5 - that does not sound like flats or houses. Now I would have thought, in fact, it sounds like flats or houses that's the property that cannot be moved.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Under current circumstances, that's correct. And it appears that my questions on this may have confused the issue and I apologise for that. I'll actually move on to a different area.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, you've described that Serbs left -- there was some Serbs who left the municipality of Foca. Would you agree that Muslims also left the municipality of Foca?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In the early days, both went away.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, and you would agree that in May and June of 1992, and past then, there were Muslims who were held in different locations in Foca municipality against their will?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: It is quite possible - I'm not denying that - but can you please be more specific? Can you draw my attention to something, let's say, fields, meadows or any other localities, I'd like to be asked about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Certainly. First let's talk about KP Dom which you referred to in paragraph 20 of your statement. In fact, in paragraph 20, you talk about the -- and I believe the quote is "the KP Dom incident." Can you tell us what you mean by "incident" just briefly?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please show me this paragraph in order to avoid any confusion? If you are referring to these first days, the 8th or, rather, 7th and 8th of April, all detainees were released from the KPZ and they scattered around, climbing a slope and eventually reaching a forest, a thick forest, and that is when they were being pursued. There were various inmates there and they were coming from various ethnic backgrounds. After that --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your statement is currently on the screen and you lead off that the first line of that sentence, "As for the Foca KP Dom incident," is that what you referring to early in April?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: All right. You would agree that certainly by the 9th of June, 1992 --

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: They were released before that, the inmates, those who happened to be there. This refers, however, to the appointment of Mr. Krnojelac as the warden, as it was called at the time, of the KPZ, and I can explain that, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I'm just trying to understand the context for paragraph 20. When you refer to "incident," you're referring to 7th or 8th April, 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: And their release, yes, you're absolutely right.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: All right. But, sir, would you agree that Muslims were held in KP Dom against their will in May and June of 1992 as well? And ...

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot say decisively when was it that the Muslims left the KP Dom because the separation line on the 14th, if I'm not wrong, when Krnojelac was appointed warden, the separation line ran near the health centre which is far away from the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm stopping you again, Witness. The question simply was whether Muslims were held in KP Dom against their will in May and June 1992. Were they, were they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were brought in, I suppose, against their will. I think that investigations were conducted in those months whether they had weapons or whether they were involved in any procurement of weapons, and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You were not asked about that. Carefully listen to Ms. Bibles' next question.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 31399 on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, this is a 9 June 1992 request from the temporary warden of KP Dom to the War Presidency of Foca. First, you will see that it reflects that a week prior to this request, the same request had been made to the Foca Crisis Staff. If you look in the second paragraph we read that the request advises that "470 prisoners were captured during war operations" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is "persons".

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Yes, persons. "470 persons captured during war operations and 10 persons of Serbian nationality are at the Foca penal and correctional institution. There are also eight convicted persons who had been serving sentences in before. In addition, in the past month and a half, around 550 captured persons have passed through this institution." So would you agree that these -- sir, wait.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please listen to the question first.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Based on the fact that Serbian individuals are named separately, that these numbers refer to non-Serbs?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
