utterances.text: It is possible, but I wasn't following this situation. I wasn't in charge of these affairs except to comply with requests for food or hygiene products to be supplied. I'm not familiar with this document. I see that there's some weaponry mentioned for security purposes. I don't know about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: We do see that there's a request to lay mines along the fence for part of KP Dom. And I was going ask if you knew whether these were provided?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: If they made such a request, they probably got it from the army and probably was on the way to the forest where they were released --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, do you know anything about it, or are you just guessing about what may have happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I absolutely never saw this paper and, quite simply, it's new to me. I don't know. I never went to the KP Dom because there was no need for me to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you do not know anything about the mines, whether they were provided or not, and whether minefields were laid?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is quite possible but I cannot claim that it is true with any certainty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, then -- is it your position -- is it your position that during the war time KP Dom was a military prison?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Only at the beginning did it serve for the purposes of interrogating the detainees. After that, it was transferred under the jurisdiction of the Ministry of Justice, as it belonged to it before, because normally Ministry of Justice is in charge of correctional and penal facilities. And I'm talking about the government of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I'll ask if we could go to the last page of this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be a bit more clear about, he said started under the Ministry of Justice; they ended under the Ministry of Justice. Who was responsible in between?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Apparently the domestic structures. Now, believe me, I have to think carefully about this in order not to make any mistake. It could have only been the local military structure, whether at the TO level when these people were taken in for questioning --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What could have been the case is different from: Do you know who was in charge.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mean in the prison or ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, was it --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The person in charge of the prison was Mr. Krnojelac, who was a mathematics teacher and reserve first class captain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was it under control of the military, or was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was appointed on behalf of the civilian authorities in order to preserve the property that was within the compound of the KP such as farm facilities, et cetera, because he was a conscientious person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Was the military in any way involved in guarding prisoners or in the prison administration? If you know, tell us; if you don't know, tell us as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I know is that -- that there were guards who basically used to work at the KP Dom before the war. That's as much as I know. Whether new ones were added to them but I don't think that they came from the military. I believe that the guards who worked at the KP Dom before the war continued to work there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What you think and what you believe, we're not interested in. What you know we're interested in. And the fact that guards served before the war in KP Dom were still there doesn't mean in any way that others, such as the military, were not there. Just for you to know that your answer does not really answer my question. Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I have one follow-up question. Who was the superior of Mr. Krnojelac? To whom did he report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was supposed to submit reports to the Ministry of Justice. Therefore, I think that it was Mr. Mandic, if I'm not mistaken. Minister Mandic. The minister of justice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You believe that. Thank you. And an additional question. On page 48, lines 20 to 22, you were asked: "Is it your position that during the war time, KP Dom was a military prison?" Your answer was: "Only at the beginning did it serve for the purposes of interrogating the detainees," which was not a proper answer to that question. But then you continue: "After that, it was transferred under the jurisdiction of the Ministry of Justice." What do you mean by "after that"? What time-period are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, in view of the system of communications, I cannot say exactly which period was covered by the Ministry of Justice. They were placed under their jurisdiction, but I cannot give you any specific time-frame because I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And before, it was placed under the jurisdiction of the Ministry of Justice, it was under -- or under whose jurisdiction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of the Territorial Defence or units of the Serbian army or the operational staff, as it was initially called, until regular units were set up on the 28th of June, which is St. Vitus Day, of 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have one very short question. You told us that you were a member of the Crisis Staff. Were you ever a member of the War Commission?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Frankly speaking, the War Commission, I think, appeared in 1995, during the bombing of Foca. Before that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, first of all, I didn't ask you that. But if you look at the document we previously had on our screen which was a document dated the 18th of June, it is addressed to the operate staff of the Executive Committee of the Serbian municipality of Foca but it originates from the Serbian municipality of Foca War Commission. So that's 1992 and not 1995. Were you, in 1992, ever a member of the War Commission?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. The commissioner was Mr. Maksimovic at the time, whereas, I operated at the level of the Executive Committee. We did meet, that is true, but I wasn't a member of the commissioner's office. I apologise. I thought that you were referring to the Presidency. That's why I mentioned the year 1995 when the Presidency was set up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honours, I do note the clock.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps it's the appropriate time to take a break. Could the witness be escorted out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will resume at 25 minutes past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bibles, we were -- we have intervened quite a bit. Could you give us an indication as to how much time you will still knead.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I will finish in the first half of this session. We have advised the Defence to be prepared for the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that information.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, while we have a minute here, I would tender 31399 which is the document on our screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 31399 receives number P6837, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, just to briefly close the last area of testimony. Is it correct that you never went to KP Dom during the war?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I should have been clearer. If I understand your questions [sic] prior to the break, do you know much about what happened at KP Dom during the war?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: In statements of different witnesses, I saw that there had been torture and probably mistreatment of individuals. Perhaps they were beaten with truncheons, et cetera. But could I not understand that baseball bats existed in Foca because that is virtually impossible, really. I mean, well, all the rest --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: To clarify, have you -- did you go to KP Dom during the war.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Did you go to the KP Dom during the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not go --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- but at the request made, I did provide food and also products for hygiene.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This was not the question. You did not go to the KP Dom. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir I'd like to shift topics. If we could have D576 on our screens, please. Sir, this is a surrender of weapons agreement with the Muslims in the village of Trosanj. Were you involved in the negotiations with that village?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And another one too, but this one as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Do you recognise your signature on the document on the screen?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Certainly. Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And this is your only evidence of personal knowledge with respect to this village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I talked to people. There were three of them there, in the presence of the territorial commander of the Serb army, and we agreed on what we agreed upon, as you can see from these conclusions, positions, whatever you wish. You can ask me further questions. I also talked to the village of Jelec; the representatives, that is.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Did you sign a similar document with them?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I think so, but I haven't kept it. I think it's only logical that I signed that one too, if I signed this one. The essence would basically be the same.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: You've described that the commander -- the territorial commander of the Serb army was present. Can you tell us who that was?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: No, not territorial. Local unit. Well, let's say, was it a battalion or something like that?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And perhaps I can correct this. At --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We do not hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, you were in the transcript quoted as saying: "I talked to people. There were three of them there, in the presence of the territorial commander of the Serb army, and we agreed on what we agreed upon." Who were you talking about as the commander?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I think his last name is Vukovic, if I'm not mistaken. After all, there is this distance involved, but I think it's Vukovic. I think his last name is Vukovic. He just attended, and he brought people there to talk. This happened in my office.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Could that have been Zoran Vukovic?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know, believe me. In that hierarchy of theirs there are quite a few of Vukovics. I mean, it's a very frequent surname, Vukovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Did you have any more personal interaction with the villagers from Trosanj after you signed this agreement?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: No. Please, I kindly ask you to focus on this ... in one of these points, I say --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness. Witness --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're not to suggest what Ms. Bibles should focus at. Please answer the questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If I understand correctly, your answer to the question --

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I did not contact. I did not contact --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. We'll move on now. You've repeated several times in your testimony and what's in paragraph 18 of your statement regarding Serbs leaving Foca at the beginning of the war. So I'd like to review something with you from 1993. If we can have 65 ter 2370, please. If we could go to page 24 in the English and page 17 in the original. Sir, this is a transcript from the 26th Assembly Session of the Republika Srpska which was held on the 2nd of April, 1993. We're going to a statement or a speech made by Petko Cancar. And, sir, the section for you that I would first like to look at begins -- it's at the beginning of the last paragraph, I believe, in the original language. And I believe we may need to go to the next page in the English yes, and halfway down the page in the English section where he states: "Fellow delegates" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You should direct the witness to the B/C/S portion that seems to be the third paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Should be the beginning of that third paragraph, sir. Do you see it there, "fellow delegates".

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. "Gentlemen, members of parliament," if that's it. This is Cancar's address.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: He states: "Fellow delegates, how can I explain this to myself, and especially convince Serbs in Foca that Foca can be green, when the whole territory of Foca municipality," and I won't go into the areas "the largest municipality in the former Bosnia and Herzegovina, and every part of it is in the hands of Serbs." And then at the bottom of this paragraph, I believe in both versions, we'll be looking at the section that begins: "This message obliges ..." Have you found that in the original text, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment. I'm trying. I've read it to the end here.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: All right. At the bottom of this page, he finishes his statement by saying: "This message obliges both this high body and me as their representative from Foca, and I will behave in accordance to their wishes, because there is only one people living on the territory of Foca, and there is only one religion practiced there ..." And I'll finish the quote there. Sir, by April of 1993, is it true that there was only one people living in Foca?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think that that is true. But in terms of a majority, yes. In terms of a majority, yes. But it's not absolutely correct. There were mixed marriages and let's not go into all that now. As far as I'm concerned, it's fine, but ...

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: But this is his statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it true -- is it true that the change in the ethnic composition of the municipality was so dramatic that the name of the town of Foca was changed to reflect the new ethnic composition?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: This was an unnecessary and unprincipled action because everyone knew --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, no one asked you to comment. First question is: Whether --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the composition of the municipality, the ethnic composition was so dramatic that the name of the municipality was changed to reflect that. Was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think that that was the reason. I can give an explanation.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's wait whether Ms. Bibles asks you for an explanation.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Was the name of Foca town changed to a new name.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I understood that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: That was not my question --

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think that that was the main reason.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: What is the new name?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Oh yes, yes, it was changed, yes. The name was Srbinje.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: That means that those who proposed that -- let my say straight away that I was against that for other reasons to have it rhyme you see, Trebinje --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No one asked you whether you were in favour or against. You were asked what Srbinje means. That's the question, what Srbinje means.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's a noun, a name for the town that would correspond to Trebinje, then Ljubinje, then Srbinje. That would be it. That would be the analogy. Nothing else. I don't think that anybody thought about the people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It has got nothing to do with Serbdom. It's like Trebinje and like Ljubinje. It's got nothing to do with Serbdom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the very name, that part has been inserted. That is true. It is part of the word, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That was -- the meaning of the word was the only thing you were asked for. Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And, sir, I'd last like to go to -- if we could pull -- go to P355, page 66 in the English and in the original. Sir, what you're about to see on the screen is a notebook entry from Ratko Mladic. This is a recording in that notebook that he made in Foca at a meeting on September -- 17 September 1992. Now, sir, we see that Miroslav Stanic is reflected to be the head of the War Presidency. And if we look down where there's a little symbol of -- kind of a star next to it or an asterisk, we see the notation -- let's see. I'm sorry, the second one: "Foca was supposed to be the second Islamic centre for Muslims" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No -- no speaking. No -- no conversations at a volume which is audible for others. Could you please resume, Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: "Foca was supposed to be the second Islamic centre for Muslims in Europe. "The population of Foca before the war was 42.000, of which number around 51 per cent were Muslims, and 49 per cent Serbs and Montenegrins? "Now the percentage of Serbs in Foca is 99 per cent." Now, sir, it's true that Foca became a Serb municipality; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: It would seem that way on the basis of these figures. It wasn't 42; it was 41.513 but that doesn't really mean much in the terms of this question. Now, what else? Miroslav Stanic. That is his view.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: 51, 49, it would roughly be around that. Yes, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: The question was whether Foca municipality became a Serb municipality.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: The figures show that, yes. According to Mr. Stanic's comment.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have to further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Bibles. One question. You are referring to Mr. Stanic's comment. Do you challenge that, at that point in time, the percentage of Serbs in Foca was 99 per cent?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It doesn't change anything if it's a percentage point up or down, but that would be it, roughly. I mean, 1 percentage point up or down, it doesn't mean much in this counting. That would be it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So it had become predominantly Serb?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At that time, yes. Today that is no longer the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, any questions in re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A few, Your Honour, with your leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, Mr. Mladjenovic, you were asked about talks with the delegation of the village of Trosanj. This is what I'm interested in: Could you tell the Court whether during these talks there was any mention of disarming the residents of the village of Trosanj and the surrounding area, irrespective of people's ethnic affiliation?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What were the conclusions in relation to disarmament?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: These papers show that all Muslims and Serbs were asked to disarm. Also, they were supposed to be given certificates for the weapons that they had and, when the conditions are right, these weapons would be returned. I received information after a few days that the agreement had been violated, that they started concealing weapons in the trash and so on and so forth under somebody's influence. Because these people told me many truths. Well, I don't think that this Court would be interested in all of that. But it was true. It was true.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let me just stop you for a moment here. And could we look at D576 once again in e-court. In a moment, you will have this agreement before you. In paragraph 1, there is a reference to the hand-over of weapons of all Muslims. And in paragraph 2, the hand-over of weapons of all Serbs. And there is this additional point: Those who are not engaged in military formations?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I shall slow down. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: This is what I would be interested in having you tell the Court. This part of the sentence and this part of the conclusion about the hand-over of weapons of Serbs who are not engaged in military formations.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Well, these are rural households. Middle-aged persons. And this pertains to all people who possess weapons, personally or perhaps who had been issued with weapons. You see? The reserve force of the Territorial Defence, Serbs and Muslims had long-barrelled weapons distributed to them and also the police on both sides. They had weapons issued to them from the police stations. So it has to do with everybody. And, of course, these papers, these certificates, would be issued so that all weapons could be returned to both once the conditions are right. I hope that I'm clear now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: At the moment when you were reaching this agreement, was there any information to the effect that in the village of Trosanj there were persons who were not registered residents of that village?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: That can be assumed on the basis of everything that followed but, of course, I had no idea and I made no such assumption. Later on, when they gave up or, I don't know, when they started putting this away, then I mean, really, from the leader of that unit I heard about that. I also talked to Jelec quite a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: With Mr. Ljubo Ninkovic along parallel lines. He was their neighbour and he was an influential man in Sarajevo. However, the essence is that Major Besevic ruined this agreement, as a matter of fact, weapons were to be collected, and this did start and he came in a helicopter and he ruined everything. He was a major, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, please let me clarify one matter. Mr. Mladjenovic, you said so it -- the disarming of people, it has to do with everybody. According to this, can you explain the difference in the wording between paragraph 1 and paragraph 2? Why is it written differently?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To tell you quite frankly, I and these people made no objections. I mean, quite simply, we decided that it would pertain to both peoples, both communities, and perhaps it was just reinforced, highlighted, that both should be disarmed. That is my understanding of it and I think that that was what we meant, in essence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can you explain the difference. In paragraph 1 the Muslims had to hand over legal and illegal weapons. In paragraph 2, the Serbs had to surrender their weapons, if they were not engaged in military formations. This is slightly different. Why?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct that it's different. As a matter of fact, I assume that even Muslims I mean, some of them, were in military formations. Then also the Serbs probably were in some military formations. However those who were not, then this pertained to them. To both. And both, if they were formations -- but to what degree, I don't know. I mean, I don't know how many participated. On both sides.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You signed this agreement. Why didn't you write it in a --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... way pertaining to both peoples.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I understood that it pertains equally to both peoples. It could have been phrased in a sentence, in one sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But I take it --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] People signed it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I take it it was not. And, Mr. Stojanovic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have another question in relation to the same. What was the authority of the civilian authorities of the Serb municipality of Foca which was unilaterally proclaimed by Serbs, if I understand you well, to receive weapons from the Muslims? Why would not the Serbs have to hand over their weapons to the -- to the Bosniak or Muslim authorities of Foca? What was the basis for this authority?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me tell you this. Location-wise, in the early days of war, and you can see that this was happening on the 24th of April, which means that war was well advanced, and people tried to save what was saveable. Jelec, Trosanj, all these areas are rural areas. However, the civilian authorities had the task in that period and there were quite a few Muslims there then, was to first and foremost to preserve peace and then protect property from all kinds of revenge, which is characteristic of the people from the Balkans to seek revenge whenever someone got killed. And also to preserve energy because we had a chronic shortage of electricity for many years. That was the first investment that was made in Republika Srpska. So there was a vast array of actions to recommend the protection of property belonging to both communities, to seal all the flats, et cetera. However, when it comings to torching, that's a different story, but I am open to any questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not a real answer to my question but I try to rephrase it again. What was it that the Serb authorities could impose these rules on predominantly Muslim villages? What was their authority to do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was not an imposition. It was a rather an intention to preserve and protect the local inhabitants. Because all -- both the town and village leaders had fled. That's the point. And you can find this in various documents originating from the Muslim side, not from me. Believe me, they all fled. Nobody expelled them, and then the people kept leaving, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, if you remember, in 1992, what was the area code number for Foca?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: The area code number for Foca I think was 071. Believe, I'm not quite -- postal area code was 71330. As far as the telephone area code is concerned, believe me, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. I'm not going to ask you any further questions about this because I wanted to show you a document anyway. What I want to ask you now is: To your recollection, with regard to the first days of war in Foca, that is to say, after the 8th of April, 1992, who exerted physical and actual control over the KP Dom in Foca?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Which date?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: 8th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Definitely Muslim units because Donje Polje was at least 80 per cent populated by Muslims which is from the second Cehotina Bridge, from the blue sky-scraper to the hospital, but I would say seven or eight days. Maybe if you give me time to think about it, I can put it more correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we now have in e-court P985. P985.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let's look at paragraph 2. This is a document dating from 1998, sent by the warden, Zoran Sekulovic of the Ministry of Justice in which he informs the Ministry of Justice that until 18th of April, 1992, the Green Berets were at the KP Dom in Foca and as of the 18th of April, 1992, the mopping-up and cleaning -- and clearing of the facility started and the collection of the strewn documents. In that respect, the ministry introduced work obligation at the KP Dom, starting from 20th of April, 1992. Does this document refresh your memory with regard to these affairs? And would you agree with this position expressed by Zoran Sekulovic concerning the time lines when the Muslim forces were in charge of the KP Dom, physically and militarily?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Obviously I was close but I didn't dare to say because I'm not sure. That was the second warden of the KP Dom after the dismissal of Mr. Krnojelac who went to work as a principal of the school and what happened later everybody knows. Probably this option is feasible but I didn't want to make any conjectures because I wasn't quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: One more question regarding this document. The experience and the knowledge that you acquired and which you explained to the Prosecutor during the cross-examination with regard to the release of all inmates from the KP Dom Foca, did it take place prior to the 18th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: You mean the pre-war composition?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'll rephrase my question. The convicts who were incarcerated in KP Dom Foca, did they leave, did they escape, were they released from the KP Dom before 18th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Even before the 8th, because the pursuit continued on the 5th or 6th. Some of them were caught and then they went in circles to Pus [phoen], but I don't want to tire you. But they were released.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I inquire with the parties what is the dispute that is covered by your questions? Is it part of the Prosecution's case that up till the 8th April there was not a mixed population of detainees? I gained the impression that the Prosecution's case is about the detention of Muslims and non-Serbs after that period of time, once Serbs had taken control. So what's the relevance of what happened before? And who escaped or did not escape? It seems not to be part of this case, Mr. Stojanovic. The witness, again and again, referred to it. Not asked about it but ... Could you tell us what is the dispute between you and Ms. Bibles in this respect?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what I think, but Ms. Bibles and I can clarify this issue. Because in one of the previous testimonies in this courtroom, a question was raised as to who was the one who released the convicts from the prison in Foca. If that is not in dispute, then -- and if we agree that the Muslim authorities were in charge of KP Foca, I have no need to put this question.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, my only question to the witness regarding -- or the direction for KP Dom was that he mentions an incident in his statement. I simply wanted to determine whether that was relevant to the indictment. It wasn't. And so I moved on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Stojanovic, perhaps it is advisable to respond to the Prosecution's case rather than to respond to the unsolicited remarks made by the witness. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Does that mean, Your Honours, that we don't have to dovetail this issue with the Prosecution? If that is not deemed to be relevant, I'm ready to accept it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mladjenovic, I'm going to finish with one more question. You were showing a document relating to the appointment of individuals as -- or the individual as the director on the Official Gazette of Republika Srpska. The question is: The Crisis Staff of the local authorities has any authority with regard to the procedure of appointing a director of a public institution, such as the Official Gazette of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Let me tell you straight away, it's news to me that they appealed to the Crisis Staff. However, the practice was if he started working on the 19th of April, 1992, the Executive Committee had to receive all the nominations for candidates, and then the ministry had to be involved and the Executive Committee had to give its approval.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm again interrupting. The question was to allow this person to move out from Foca. It doesn't say anything about any authority to appoint, so it's beside the point raised by the Prosecution. I must say that it wasn't entirely clear what then was the relevance the Prosecution found in this document because the simple thing was: Would you allow him to leave and come to Pale. Nothing about the appointments. Only the reason why they wanted him to leave. So, therefore, questions about authority are not triggered by the cross-examination. Apart from that, totally irrelevant. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with this, I conclude re-direct examination of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I am grateful to Mr. Mladjenovic on behalf of the Defence team of General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Have the questions by the Defence triggered any need for further questions, Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since the Bench also has no questions for you, Mr. Mladjenovic, this concludes your testimony in this court. I'd like to thank you very much for coming a long way to The Hague and for having answered, sometimes even a bit more, than that the questions that were put to you by the parties and by the Bench, and I wish you a safe return home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Orie, if you can just indulge me by giving me 20 seconds I would like do greet everyone in the courtroom, to wish them --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There's no need do that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I'm not referring to anyone specifically.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I think none of anyone sitting here is waiting for you to greet them. If you want to greet anyone, you can do it once you've left this courtroom in the way which you consider the most appropriate way. You may now follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is the ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, wouldn't it be better to take the break now and then to call the next witness after the break so that you have time until quarter past or at least not to quarter past until five past and we would then start with the cross-examination. I see from the body language of Mr. Mladic that he agreed to take the break a bit earlier. We'll take a break and resume at 25 minutes to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is the Defence ready to call its next witness? Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, our next witness is Tomislav Savkic. And we explained the reasons why we are not calling Witness Lelek at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber has received that information and fully accepts the steps taken and the change in the order of appearance of these witnesses. Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps I could try to clean up something from the last witness and that is I had intended to tender Petko Cancar's speech at the assembly, which we reviewed. I would simply tender pages 124 and 25 of 65 ter 2370.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Isn't it true that you read all of what you wanted to draw -- but perhaps you read only a selection of lines --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- from the totality of his speech. One second. Mr. Stojanovic, would you have any objections against this selection being tendered?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have you uploaded the selected portions and -- separately. Yes. And the number -- separately I see Ms. Stewart is concerned whether --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: It will be 2370A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but it has not been uploaded yet.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: It has not been uploaded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, then, it'll be uploaded under that number: 2370A. Madam Registrar, could you already reserve a number for that.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 2370A once uploaded receives number P6838, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That number is reserved until the uploading is complete.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Savkic. Before you give evidence, the Rules require that you make a solemn declaration, the text of which is now handed out to you. I'd like to invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Savkic. Please be seated. Mr. Savkic, you will first be examined by Mr. Stojanovic. You will find him to your left. Mr. Stojanovic is counsel for Mr. Mladic. Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Savkic.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: For the record, could you please slowly tell us your full name.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC
utterances.text: Tomislav Savkic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Savkic, have you given a statement to the Defence team of General Mladic, specifically to me, and provided answers to the questions that I sent you in writing?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we now call up 65 ter document 1D01771.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, in front of you, you can see the cover page of the statement. I'm asking you if this is your signature?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we please now look at the last page of this document. Mr. Savkic, the signature and the date entered on this page, is that your handwriting?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you be so kind to tell us during proofing for your appearance, you indicated to me yesterday and last night that certain amendments or corrections need to be made in your statement.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, let us look at paragraph 29 of the witness's statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In the sentence which reads: "A proposal was made to establish a working group consisting of six most distinguished representatives of Serbs and Muslims," did you tell me that what is missing here is six distinguished representatives of Serbs and Muslims each?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that can be seen in the protocol that there were six representatives from each side.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, for that reason, for the clarity of record, let us say that this sentence now should read as follows: "A proposal was made to establish a working group consisting of six most distinguished representatives of Serbs and Muslims each ..." Now, is this consistent with what you told us?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us now look at paragraph 50 of your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just for the sake of precision, in B/C/S because the English version is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The place name in B/C/S it says Pioke, whereas you say the correct name is Pijuke, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. After we have made these two corrections and after you have made a solemn declaration to speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth, if I were to put the same questions to you, would you provide the same answers as the ones contained in your statement?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think that this is a good time to tender this witness's statement, 65 ter 1D01771, into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D1771 receives number D699, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D699 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, at this point along with this statement, I would suggest that four documents mentioned in this statement be also admitted in evidence, which have 65 ter number 1D02321, 1D02322, 1D03094, and 1D03095.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. We would object only to one. 1D03094, which is a statement by another person, as we indicated in our response to the 92 ter motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, what's the reason why we have to receive that document which is a statement by another witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the reason that guided us to move to include this statement is relevant for this case and it pertains primarily to the status and position of the person who made the statement, as well as the contents of his statement in which he described the same events that this witness is going to testify to, and these events were, indeed, covered by the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now these are not the criteria for admission as an associated exhibit, Mr. Stojanovic, isn't it? It should be indispensable and we should be unable to understand the testimony of this witness without that -- without that associated exhibit. What is there then -- I suggest that we -- that you perhaps deal with the matter as suggested by the Prosecution, that you elicit evidence from the witness in relation to matters related to the same matters this statement of Mr. Sulejmanovic deals with and we deal with whether they are indispensable and necessary to understand the ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This statement is given to whom exactly, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This statement was given to the public security station in Milici on the 31st of May, 1993, to the witness who appeared in this case some ten days ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Which means that it is not directly subject to Rule 92 bis or ter. Mr. Traldi, you were on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I agree with that. However we don't see any reason to believe this witness has a basis for knowledge considering this was a person who had been taken prisoner by Serb forces during the war. We don't see any assurances that this was taken in a manner free from coercion and consequently -- and beyond that we don't find it integral and indispensable to this statement. So our submission isn't that it would be required to be 92 bis or ter itself, our submission is that it does not satisfy the test for admission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 92 bis or 92 ter is usually used for statements taken for the purposes of this tribunal and that's a practice that the Prosecution has applied continuously. It was objected to by the Defence who, by the way did exactly the same, and then -- so therefore for the time being, there are no objections to three of them. We'll deal with them. We'll see how your examination-in-chief develops in relation to this -- the events which are covered by this statement by Mr. Sulejmanovic, as well -- at least as far as we were told at this moment because we have not looked into it. Madam Registrar, 1D02321 would receive number ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Number D700, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D700 is admitted. 1D02322 would receive number ....

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D701. Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D701 is admitted. 1D03095 would receive number ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D702, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. We'll further wait for the developments in relation to paragraph 42 and the other document you intended to have admitted as an associated exhibit, Mr. Stojanovic. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your leave, Your Honour, I would like to read the summary of today's witness's statement. Witness Tomislav Savkic has a degree in electrical engineering and during 1992 he was appointed commander of the Defence of the Milici Boksit mine. From the 1st of November, 1992, he took over as commander of the 1st Infantry Battalion Milici and from 1st of November 1993 he was elected president of the Municipal Assembly of Milici and he remained in that position until the end of the war. He testifies about interethnic problems in the area of Vlasenica after the breakup of Yugoslavia, about the constitution of authorities in the municipality of Vlasenica, about disputes concerning the division of departments, and having authority over the municipality. He was familiar with the arming of the Muslims, the obstruction of mobilisation by the political leadership of the Muslims, as well as the deterioration in the security situation because of a series of incidents initiated by Muslims already from the second half of 1991. The political leaderships of the ruling parties tried to have a territorial separation in a peaceful way and to have new municipalities constituted. Along those lines, on the 13th of April, 1992, the Municipal Assembly of Vlasenica, through a conclusion of its own, adopted the agreement on the territorial separation and constitution of new municipalities but after they received information to the effect that Muslims were preparing an all-out attack against Vlasenica, the units of the JNA and a company of the TO from Sekovici entered town without any fighting. Muslims left Vlasenica in three stages, starting from mid-1991, and especially after the 21st of April, 1992, when Serb refugees started arriving in Vlasenica from different municipalities that were under the control of the Muslim authorities. Parallel to this process, Muslim paramilitary formations carried out several sabotage operations, and Serb civilians and employees of the Boksit mine were the victims. The witness speaks about his knowledge on the establishment of the Susica centre, and the clashes around the villages of Drum, Pijuke, Gradina and Zaklopaca and the fighting that took place between the VRS and the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina before the safe areas of Srebrenica and Zepa are declared. Finally, he speaks about his knowledge concerning armed struggle of the Milici brigade and the other parts of the armed forces of the RS with the column of the 28th Division of the BH army, the information that he received from different sources on the number of casualties in the column of the 28th Division of the BH army along the route of their movement and breakthrough. And, finally, the information that he was given in 1998 by the representative of the International Committee of the Red Cross that 2.600 entire bodies or body parts of participants in the column were found and collected. That would be the summary of this witness's statement, Your Honours, and with your leave, I'd like to put a few questions to hmm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, could we now please take a look at D699 together, and could you please focus on paragraph 30 where you speak about this agreement, about the territorial separation in the municipality of Vlasenica and the constitution of new municipalities. In view of what you referred to in paragraph 29 of your statement, could you tell the Court whether you were one of the participants in these talks?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC
utterances.text: Yes. I am under number 4. In Serbian, the page in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell the Court whether these talks between the Serb and Muslim people in Vlasenica resulted in some specific agreement on the peaceful resolution of the problems that had accumulated?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you are referring to number 4. Number 4 of what? You have apparently paperwork before you which you're supposed not to have. If there's any document you'd like to consult, you should ask permission for that. That's one. And, Mr. Stojanovic, you seemed to easily accept that answer so apparently you know what the witness is talking about. Or aren't you?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Quite frankly, I don't know, Your Honours. I can just assume what this is about, and I thought --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, the witness says: Yes, I'm under number 4, in Serbian, the page in Serbian. And then you move on. And you do not know what the witness is referring to. It is not only your questions that are important but the answers are important to be understood as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have no problem with asking that, asking what this is about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, you should have done that before I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Paragraph 4 of what, Witness? Number 4.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not a paragraph. I was precise. I said that in the signature, I am under number 4. As for the representatives of the Serb people --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What document are you talking about? That's unclear to us. We do not know what document you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm speaking about the document from this paragraph. That is the protocol of the agreement on the separation in the municipality of Vlasenica. It is written here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's clear now. But we haven't seen that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have this intention and I have notified my colleagues of the Prosecution, I intend to use this document and then, probably, it would have become clearer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I wonder if the witness has a different document in front of him on the screen than we and the parties. Are you referring to a document on the screen in front of you or a different document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The lawyer, Mr. Stojanovic told me nicely to focus on paragraph 30, and paragraph 30 starts as follows: "This agreement ..." Well, that was the lawyer's question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me try to cut matters short. I do understand that paragraph 30 refers to a document, a document which is not before the Chamber but a document of which you apparently have a copy before you. Now, Mr. Stojanovic, the proper way of dealing with it is to show the document to the Chamber as well, because whatever you agree with -- about with the Prosecution, the Chamber still has a role to play in this courtroom as well. So try to get matters organised so that the evidence comes to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just to have the record be completely clear, we had understood that he intended to use the agreement, as Mr. Stojanovic has stated. We hadn't understood or agreed to the Defence having physical copies of documents we haven't seen with him and we'd just request eventually to be provided with a copy of the documents that the witness has with him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Stojanovic, get organised and proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Agreed, Your Honour. In order to be quite clear, could we now have document 65 ter 02894 in e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, this document that you see before you now, is that the document that you've been speaking about in your statement, in paragraph 30?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please look at the last page of this document in B/C/S and in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you whether my assumptions were correct when you mentioned that you were the fourth signatory of this document.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC
utterances.text: Yes, as far as the representatives of the Serb people are concerned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In order to avoid whatever confusion in English, it's not the last page of the document, it's the semi-last page. It's page 6 out of seven. But having corrected this, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Under number 4, the name, Tomo Savkic, does it correspond to your name, Tomislav Savkic, and is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's my signature. It can be seen here. And we Serbs otherwise when people have longer names, then they are shortened, like elsewhere in the world, too. So instead of Tomislav, it says Tomo.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you also present at the Municipal Assembly of Vlasenica when the question of the possibility of adopting this agreement was discussed?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What was the objective of such a signed agreement between the representatives of the Serb and Muslim peoples in Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC
utterances.text: It is best stated in paragraph 8 of this agreement. It is precisely on this page where the signatures are. So it's page 7. However, it's black from what I see here, but I have the original right in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In order to be quite clear, it is page 6 in the English version. And I would like to ask you to tell us in your own words what the ultimate objective of this agreement was.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC
utterances.text: The ultimate objective of this agreement was as follows: The situation that then prevailed in the municipality of Vlasenica was supposed to be dealt with as follows. The administration should fully function or, rather, self-administration or self-government. Because the then-leadership of the municipality, already from the month of July 1991, was not in a position to carry out its basic functions. As a matter of fact, all of them, all 21 of them, from the lowest-ranking official to the president of the Executive Council, they had to carry pistols or revolvers, and we said here quite clearly we are doing this on the best possible basis for the people, in terms of the functioning of the government and administration, and that can be seen from this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At the session of the assembly that was held on the 13th of April, 1992, actually, in paragraph 30, you refer to that assembly. Were there any objections there, in view of this protocol? Was it adopted through a conclusion adopted by the assembly?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was adopted through a conclusion adopted by the assembly. I think it is conclusion number 2. However - however - there are four other conclusions that are very important as well. But it was adopted without any alterations.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have document 65 ter 1D03502 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, is this the document that you spoke of in your statement and that you are speaking of today in this courtroom?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: This paragraph, or Article 2 of the conclusions, is that precisely what you were speaking about today in response to my questions?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC
utterances.text: Yes. That can be seen from the meaning, I hope that it was translated well into English.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, would like to tender these through documents 65 ter 02894, and 1D03502. Could they please be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: No objections, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 2894 receives number D703. And document 1D3502 receives number D704, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D703 and D704 are admitted into evidence. One -- one question. Was there any dispute about what we heard about, that there had been a meeting and agreement and that the agreement was adopted by the municipal assembly? Is there any dispute about those facts? Apart from any circumstances. Because they were not presented to us yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That the documents reflect what they reflect. And that the agreement was entered into, I don't believe there's a dispute about, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Stojanovic, why not explore that, rather than to spend time on it in court. Okay. Matters are as they are, sometimes. Any further questions, Mr. Stojanovic, and how much time would you still need or was this your examination-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I haven't finished, Your Honour. I have two more questions and two more documents to deal with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, think it over, overnight if these are matters in dispute, yes or no. If need be, contact Mr. Traldi on the matter, and we'll then continue tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. If there's no dispute, we will accept that with pleasure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you're duty-bound to do that, I would say, not to spend time in court on matters which are not in dispute. Mr. Savkic, we'll adjourn for the day. We'd like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.30 in this same courtroom. Meanwhile, I want to instruct you that you should not speak with anyone, or communicate with whomever, about your testimony, whether that is testimony you have given today or whether that is testimony we expect you to give tomorrow. If that's clear to you, you may follow the usher. Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. And I think I was a little bit imprecise before requesting that we eventually be provided a copy of those documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We'd like to have it before tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could we -- could the witness come back for a second - I apologise - and put on his earphones again. You are in the possession and you consulted -- you are in the possession and you consulted documents. Where do they come from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These are my personal documents. These are originals of these documents, these documents, that we talked about today. That is to say that agreement, then this decision of the municipal assembly and so on. I had bad experience in this court. I had forgeries planted on me by the Prosecution at the trial of Momo Krajisnik. So just in case, I took along the originals.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do I understand that, until now, you've only referred to this protocol and you've only consulted the protocol which you were asked about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then you should make up your mind: Either leave them in your hotel room tomorrow, or if you want to bring them, that's fine. But then you should give an opportunity to the Prosecution to look at them and they'll certainly be very careful with it. Mr. Stojanovic would then perhaps have a look at it as well, and they will be returned to you by the Victims and Witness Section before you enter court or perhaps even later this afternoon. So it's up to you whether you want to have them with you tomorrow, in which case you are invited to hand them over so that they can be inspected, or to say, I don't need them any further. And Mr. Traldi, I take it that you'll accept the witness's answer that -- I mean, if he doesn't use them, then, of course, everyone can have whatever documents he wished to have.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So could you tell us whether you want to have them available for you for consultation tomorrow? If that's the case, please hand them over temporarily to the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And could you -- and apart from that, you should already show the one document you have used today, so you should give that original for inspection - you'll get it back - for inspection to the Prosecution. And if you want to use the other ones tomorrow as well, you should give the whole bundle to the Prosecution. Yes --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When's he bringing them back to me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I take it, Mr. Traldi, that it will not take long for you to inspect them, copies can be made, and you'd be within half an hour, one hour. And then, of course, the Defence also should have an opportunity to inspect them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, I think that's reasonable, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Which means that it could be returned by approximately 4.00; Mr. Stojanovic, I'm also looking at you. You're to receive them back later this afternoon. Is that okay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Four documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Four documents. Do you have any other documents? You should leave them at home if you -- if you want to use them, if you want to consult them tomorrow, then you should give them now. If not, then, of course, take them and leave them in your hotel room. It's up to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Six. Six documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the others, you will leave in your hotel room tomorrow. Is that understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then you'll -- these six documents will be returned to you later today. Later this afternoon. Apologies for asking to you come back again. My instructions still apply.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that the parties will, without any delay, inspect the documents and take care that, with the assistance of the Registry, that they will be returned to the witness. We adjourn for the day, and we resume tomorrow, Wednesday, the 22nd of October, in this same courtroom, I, at 9.30 in the morning.
